newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close mixed ahead of key reports.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close mixed ahead of key reports.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed little changed in quiet conditions ahead of the release of key cattle-on-feed and cattle inventory reports, due at 1400 CDT on Friday.
Dealers said there was light trade in the cash market at a steady $64.00 per cwt while futures just appeared to be marking time ahead of the USDA reports.

Strength in product values boosted sentiment with USDA boxed beef cut-out values, as of 1130 CDT, up $0.42 to $0.62 per cwt. August live cattle closed down 0.025 cent at 66.550 cents with other months down 0.100 cent to up 0.275 cent.
Dealers noted the cattle-on-feed report may indicate that supplies of fed cattle will be fairly plentiful during the next month and a half.
A Reuters survey of analysts produced an average projection for cattle-on-feed in large lots in the leading seven states, as of July 1, of 115.6 percent of a year ago.

Feeder cattle futures closed mostly lower with higher CBOT corn prices weighing on the market. Strength in the cash feeder cattle market continued to support nearby months and August set a contract high of 83.050 cents before finishing 0.050 cent up at 82.800 cents.
